title: Castles and knights
examples: What was the difference between a motte and a bailey castle?
How did knights actually fight during a siege?
What did the code of chivalry mean for a knight?

explain.say: Today we will learn about castles and the knights who lived there. We will see how these structures protected people long ago.
A motte and bailey castle was built quickly for defense. The motte was a large mound of earth. The bailey was the wooden enclosure around it.
Later, people built stronger stone castles for better defense. These stone walls were much harder to break down. They showed great engineering skill.
When enemies attacked, they would try to take the castle in a siege. Defenders used arrows and boiling liquids from the battlements.
Knights were famous for their code called chivalry. This code meant they were brave and honorable soldiers. They were expected to protect the weak.
In real life, a modern fortress uses similar ideas for defense. Think about a bank vault or a secure government building.

faq.q: How long did people live in these castles?
faq.a: People lived in castles for many years, sometimes for generations. They were major centers of power and life.
asks: How long did the castle lifestyle last?

faq.a: Chivalry was an ideal, not always reality. While the code suggested honor, real battles were often very violent.
asks: Did knights always follow the rules?
What was the reality of a knight's life?

faq.q: What was the main difference between the two castle types?
faq.a: The motte and bailey used wood and earth, while stone castles used permanent, thick stone walls. Stone was much more durable.

faq.q: Did sieges always end with a big fight?
faq.a: Not always. Sometimes a siege ended because the defenders ran out of food or supplies. Starvation was a common tactic.
asks: What was the goal of a siege?
Could a castle fall without a big battle?

faq.q: What was the purpose of the moat around a castle?
faq.a: The moat was a ditch filled with water, making it very hard for attackers to reach the base of the walls. It added another layer of defense.
asks: Why was water used in defense?
Did the moat stop all attacks?

facts: Motte and bailey castles were early, temporary fortifications.
Stone castles provided much greater defense against fire and siege weapons.
Sieges involved surrounding a location to cut off supplies and escape.
Chivalry was an idealized code of conduct for knights.

quiz.say: Which structure was built first and used earth and wood?
quiz.why: This early type used readily available earth and timber for quick defense.

wrong.0: Battlements are parts of the wall, not the whole initial structure.
wrong.1: Chivalry is a code of conduct, not a physical building type.
wrong.3: Stone castles required much more time and specialized materials to build.

quiz.say: If a castle was under siege, what was a common tactic used by the attackers?
quiz.why: By blocking food and water, the defenders would eventually give up.

wrong.0: Attackers usually needed to surround the entire area, not just the gate.
wrong.1: Sieges involved many tactics, not just one type of weapon.
wrong.2: While surrender was possible, the initial goal was usually to force a fight.

quiz.say: A knight following the code of chivalry would most likely show:
quiz.why: Chivalry emphasized protecting those who could not defend themselves.

wrong.0: The code required honorable behavior even when fighting.
wrong.1: Chivalry valued skill and honor over just raw power.
wrong.2: The code demanded restraint and fairness in conduct.
